question: Is there an exact number of hairs at which a man becomes bald?
answer: Yes, says Timothy Williamson: one hair makes the difference, though nobody can know which. His 1994 book Vagueness argues that every rival view gives up ordinary logic, so the sharp line must exist, hidden from us. The law already behaves this way: one day separates a minor from an adult.
move: A line nobody can find may still be a line that matters.
ask: Where am I waiting for a clear line to appear before I act, when none ever will?
